units.label: JavaScript (ECMAScript language + browser platform APIs)
units.pins: No product pin — the language is versioned by ECMAScript edition. Node 24.19.0 (lts) and Vitest 5.0.0 / bcrypt 6.0.0 declare this track for runtime/test examples only.
units.currency: No pin governs the language itself — the checker cannot see ES-edition drift at all.
units.notes: The 'LTS' equivalent here is the ECMAScript edition ladder: ES2022 → ES2023 → ES2024 → ES2025 → ES2026 (the June 2026 edition — check it is published) plus Stage 4 proposals finished for ES2027 (tc39/proposals finished-proposals.md). Take each edition's feature list from tc39.es/ecma262 / github.com/tc39/proposals/blob/main/finished-proposals.md; for browser platform APIs (phases 10–12: events, network/storage, browser platform) use web.dev Baseline / MDN browser-compat to see what became Baseline newly/widely available in 2024–2026 (e.g. Temporal, Iterator helpers, Set methods, Promise.try, RegExp.escape, Float16Array, Error.isError, Math.sumPrecise, Uint8Array base64, import attributes, JSON modules, explicit resource management `using`, Array.fromAsync, Atomics.pause — take the real list from the sources, not this note). Phases 13–18 are DSA / machine-coding / storefront — skip them except for language features they use. 94 topics left across a 4-way split — grade unwritten syllabus items PLANNED.
